question.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/1ffc0945ea74b1bd467a0b9935ee28b88be004c18b11492d67ecdfec56e1bb09.png)

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.
question.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,3,2)$ and $Q(2,4,5).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+3t \\ 3+t \\ 2+3t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-1+3t \\ y=3+t \\ z=2+3t\end{aligned}
$$

Two source defects remain: q-105261 labels a row scaling as -1/2 although its displayed result requires +1/2; q-127043 has two mathematically correct radio choices, options 1 and 2, because opposite nonzero vectors are both parallel to the line. Its worked solution explicitly supports option 1. Independently, q-34218 has the unique decomposition b=2a1+4a2-2a3, giving product -16. In q-74558, every vector in the span has equal first and third coordinates, requiring k=0; coefficients (2,1) establish sufficiency. In q-74560, every vector in the span has third coordinate twice its first, requiring k=-24; coefficients (-2,-2) establish sufficiency. In q-105248, the first and third equations force s=1,t=-1, but these give second coordinate 6 rather than 5, so u is outside the plane. In q-105261, u=-b-2c gives st=2. The selected vectors in q-34142 and q-105291 are respectively -3a1 and a1/3. In q-34276, a3=a1-a2 proves dependence, so only III is true. In q-105315, determinant -6 proves independence, so II and III are true. Separating constants and coefficients of t gives the vector equations in q-36023 and q-127002. The coefficients of t give parallel vectors in q-32785 and q-127043. For q-32817, the image shows P=(-1,3,2) and Q=(2,4,5); Q-P=(3,1,3), giving the selected parametric equations.
